  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Texas Reverse Mortgage sale

Inherited a Home With a Reverse Mortgage? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is and work with the lender and title company on the payoff. Tell us about the house.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

When a Texas reverse mortgage comes due

Under Texas Constitution Article XVI, Sec. 50(k)(6), no payment of principal or interest is required until one of these happens:

  • all borrowers have died;
  • the homestead is sold or otherwise transferred;
  • all borrowers stop living there for more than 12 consecutive months without prior written lender approval;
  • the borrower defaults on repairs and maintenance, taxes or assessments, or insurance, commits actual fraud, or fails to maintain lien priority.

A Texas reverse mortgage must go to a borrower who, or whose spouse, is 62 or older, and it carries no recourse for personal liability against each owner and each owner's spouse (Sec. 50(k)(2) and (3)). Interest can accrue and compound during the loan term as the agreement provides (Sec. 50(m)).

What heirs can do

HUD's flyer for heirs of an FHA-insured HECM says:

  • Heirs who want to keep the home must pay the balance in full. Property taxes and insurance stay the estate's responsibility until title transfers.
  • A non-borrowing spouse may qualify for special provisions that postpone repayment, but must give the lender a Non-Borrowing Spouse Certification within 30 days of the last borrower's death, among other requirements.

Contact the lender right away. The HUD FHA Resource Center number on the flyer is (800) 225-5342. Heirs also need to settle who has authority to sell, which depends on whether there is a will. See the Texas probate process and affidavit of heirship.

Inherited a home with a HECM?
We buy as-is and can close quickly, with no commission. The title company pays off the lender from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

If the lender wants to foreclose

The lender cannot begin foreclosure until it gives notice that a ground exists and gives the borrower at least 30 days (20 days for a lien-priority default) to fix the problem, pay the debt from a sale or other sources, or give a deed in lieu of foreclosure (Sec. 50(k)(10)). Foreclosure needs a court order, except where the ground is that all borrowers have died or the home was sold or transferred (Sec. 50(k)(11)). See the Texas foreclosure process.

What we could not confirm

  • Any Texas Finance Code provision on reverse mortgages.
  • Whether HUD's later guidance changed the 2019 flyer's deadlines or extension rules, and how many extensions a lender can grant.
  • How the Texas 30-day and 20-day foreclosure notice interacts with HUD's 30-day payoff timeline.

Texas reverse mortgage FAQ

How long do heirs have to deal with a HECM?

HUD says the loan must be satisfied within 30 days of the borrower's death, and the lender may approve 90-day extensions with documentation that the estate or heirs are actively trying to sell or repay.

Can heirs sell for less than the loan balance?

HUD says that if the balance exceeds the home's value, heirs may sell for at least 95 percent of the current appraised value, and the lender accepts the net proceeds as satisfaction of the loan.

What makes a Texas reverse mortgage due?

The death of all borrowers, a sale or transfer, absence for more than 12 consecutive months without lender approval, or a default on taxes, insurance, maintenance or lien priority, or fraud (Const. art. XVI, Sec. 50(k)(6)).

Can a surviving spouse who is not on the loan stay?

HUD says special provisions may postpone repayment, but the spouse must give the lender a certification within 30 days of the last borrower's death, among other requirements.

What happens to a Texas reverse mortgage when the borrower dies?

The loan balance becomes due and payable when the last surviving borrower dies, and no more money can be advanced. HUD's flyer for heirs of an FHA-insured Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM) says the borrower makes no payments while living in the house, and the balance comes due when the borrower sells, stops using it as a primary residence, or dies.

The flyer sets a 30 day payoff period running from the death, and adds that the lender may approve 90-day extensions when the estate or heirs show they are actively trying to sell the property or repay the loan. Its date is September 2019, so ask the servicer which deadlines it is applying to your loan.

What notice must the lender send the heirs?

HUD Mortgagee Letter 2022-15 says the servicer must send a Due and Payable Notice to the estate, heirs or other party holding legal title within 30 days after it tells HUD the last surviving borrower has died. Earlier guidance started the clock at death.

The notice has to say the estate or heirs may satisfy the loan, sell the property for at least 95 percent of the appraised value, or hand the lender a deed in lieu. The letter carves out loans with a case number issued before August 4, 2014 where a surviving non-borrowing spouse exists, and sends servicers to earlier letters for those.

  • Pay the loan balance in full and keep the house.
  • Sell for at least 95 percent of appraised value when the balance is higher than the home's worth.
  • Offer the lender a deed in lieu.

Can heirs sell the house for less than the loan balance?

Yes, within HUD's rule. The flyer says that if the balance exceeds the home's value, the estate or heirs may sell for at least 95 percent of the current appraised value, and the lender will accept the net proceeds as payment in full. It adds that any transfer after death counts as a sale for this purpose.

Heirs who want to keep the home must pay off the loan balance in full. Property taxes and insurance stay the responsibility of the borrower's estate until title transfers, so keep paying them while the sale is in motion. Texas property taxes are generally due by January 31, and the Comptroller says unpaid bills turn delinquent on February 1 with penalty and interest.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What can a surviving spouse who is not on the loan do?

A non-borrowing spouse may qualify for special provisions that postpone repayment and allow the spouse to stay in the home. HUD's flyer says the spouse must give the lender a Non-Borrowing Spouse Certification within 30 days of the last surviving borrower's death, among other requirements.

Because the deadline is short, call the servicer right away. The FHA Resource Center, listed on the flyer, can be reached at (800) 225-5342, or by email at answers@hud.gov.

Who has authority to sell an inherited Texas home?

That depends on how the owner left the property, and the lender will ask for proof. The Texas State Law Library lists several routes to put title in a seller's hands.

Documents the State Law Library guide ties to inherited real property
How the owner left the housePaper recorded or used
Transfer on death deedAffidavit of death and death certificate, recorded
Estate with an executor or administratorExecutor's or administrator's deed
Muniment of titleCourt order and the will
None of the aboveAffidavit of heirship

The guide says the county cannot add heirs to the old deed. The guide gives four years from death to probate a will, and the application normally goes to the court where the person lived. A small estate affidavit is a further option for some estates, with conditions the library lists.

What conditions make a Texas reverse mortgage due earlier?

The Texas Attorney General describes a reverse mortgage as a loan for homeowners age 62 or older with enough equity, with payment deferred until the borrower dies, sells or moves out. Borrowers still pay property taxes and homeowner's insurance throughout the loan, and interest keeps accruing.

Falling behind on those costs is the usual trigger for a default. The Attorney General's page also says closing costs may be financed into the loan and that the lien is typically paid off when the home is sold. Read the loan documents for the exact default terms, and ask the servicer to list in writing every condition it relies on.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Can the lender foreclose on a reverse mortgage in Texas?

Yes, but in Texas the State Law Library says a reverse mortgage foreclosure goes through an expedited court order rather than the usual auction by power of sale. Ordinary Texas home loans follow a power-of-sale path with an auction, which is a different track.

The Library notes that after any foreclosure, a buyer facing an occupant may need an eviction case. An heir who plans to sell has more control by listing early than by waiting for the lender to act, since a sale lets the title company pay the lender from proceeds.

Where can I get free help with a reverse mortgage question?

HUD can supply a list of approved reverse mortgage counseling agencies that charge nothing or little, and the Attorney General's page lists HUD at (800) 569-4287 for that purpose. The Homeowner's HOPE Hotline, at (888) 995-4673, is another number the Attorney General's page gives for people facing foreclosure.

  • Lender or servicer: payoff figure, deadlines, extension requests.
  • HUD-approved counselor: options in plain language.
  • Texas attorney: authority to sell, estate issues, disputes.
  • Texas Attorney General: complaints about scams or loan servicing.

The Attorney General warns that scammers sometimes pass off reverse mortgages as government benefits, so do not sign anything you do not fully understand.

What should I ask the servicer before listing the house?

Start with the written payoff figure and the date it expires, since interest keeps accruing on a reverse mortgage. Ask for the appraisal the servicer will use, because the 95 percent measure in HUD's rule is tied to the appraised value, and ask who orders it and when.

  • Which deadline applies to this loan, and when did the 30 days begin?
  • What paperwork shows that an extension is granted, and for how long?
  • Which documents prove my authority to sell?
  • Will the lender accept the net proceeds as full payment if the sale price is under the balance?

Keep the answers in writing. If a servicer refuses to explain its position, a HUD-approved counselor or the Texas Attorney General's complaint process can help you press the question, and a title company handling the closing will pay the lender from the proceeds.

More questions about Texas Reverse Mortgage

How long do heirs have to pay off a HECM in Texas?

HUD's heirs flyer says 30 days from the borrower's death, with 90-day extensions the lender may approve when heirs are actively selling or repaying. Confirm the current deadline with your servicer.

Can I sell for less than the reverse mortgage balance?

Yes, for an FHA-insured HECM. HUD says heirs may sell for at least 95 percent of the current appraised value when the balance is higher, and the lender accepts net proceeds as satisfaction.

Do I owe the difference if the house sells short of the balance?

For a sale at or above 95 percent of appraised value, HUD says the lender accepts the net proceeds as satisfaction of the loan. Ask the servicer to confirm that in writing before closing.

What if my spouse was not on the loan?

A non-borrowing spouse may qualify to postpone repayment. HUD says a Non-Borrowing Spouse Certification must reach the lender within 30 days of the last borrower's death.

Who pays taxes and insurance after the borrower dies?

The borrower's estate, until title transfers, according to HUD's flyer. Unpaid Texas property taxes become delinquent after January 31 under the Comptroller's schedule.

title: Texas Mechanic's Lien on a Home: Deadlines, Homestead Rules and Selling
content:
Texas Mechanic's Lien on a Home: Deadlines, Homestead Rules and Selling

Cash Home Buyers in Texas
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Texas Mechanic's Lien on a Home: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Texas Mechanic's Lien on a Home sale
  • Turn the Texas Mechanic's Lien on a Home offer down and you owe us nothing

Contractor Lien on Your Texas House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is, including houses with recorded liens. Tell us what you found.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

To fix a mechanic's lien on a Texas homestead, the contractor and the owner must sign a written contract before work starts, both spouses must sign if the owner is married, and the contract must be filed with the county clerk. Those requirements are in Property Code Sec. 53.254. This guide covers the filing deadlines, how a lien is released and what we could not confirm about how a lien affects a sale.

Who gets a lien and when

A person has a lien if, under a contract with the owner or the owner's agent, trustee, contractor or subcontractor, the person furnishes labor or materials to build or repair an improvement (Sec. 53.021). Property Code Sec. 41.001(b)(3) says work and material encumbrances can be properly fixed on homestead property only if contracted in writing as Sec. 53.254(a), (b) and (c) provide.

For a homestead, a lien affidavit must carry the notice "THIS IS NOT A LIEN. THIS IS ONLY AN AFFIDAVIT CLAIMING A LIEN" in at least 10-point boldface at the top of the page, and the owner notice must include the statutory statement about reserving 10 percent (Sec. 53.254(f) and (g)).

Filing and suit deadlines

  • Original contractor, residential project: file the lien affidavit with the county clerk by the 15th day of the third month after the month the work was completed, terminated or abandoned (Sec. 53.052(a)).
  • Other claimants, residential project: the 15th day of the third month after the later of the month they last provided labor or materials (Sec. 53.052(c)).
  • Where: the county where the improvements are located (Sec. 53.052(e)).
  • Suit to foreclose: not later than the first anniversary of the last day the claimant could file the affidavit, extendable to the second anniversary of filing by a recorded written agreement made before the period expires (Sec. 53.158).
  • Owner retainage: the owner must reserve 10 percent of the contract price or work value during the work and for 30 days after completion (Sec. 53.101(a)).
Lien on your house?
We buy as-is, including houses with recorded liens. The title company pays valid liens from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

Getting a lien released

Within 10 days after a written request, a claimant paid with collected funds must furnish a recordable release (Sec. 53.152). A filed lien can also end by a recorded release, by the claimant failing to sue within the Sec. 53.158 period, by a recorded final judgment, by a bond, or by a recorded order removing the lien if no bond or deposit is filed within 30 days (Sec. 53.157). In a suit, a party can file a verified summary motion to remove a lien, and for a homestead the grounds include no contract executed or filed as Sec. 53.254 requires (Sec. 53.160).

What we could not confirm

  • How an unreleased lien affects a closing and how title companies handle it. No statute text we opened says so.
  • The notice-of-claim deadlines in Secs. 53.056 and 53.057, and whether the 2025 legislature changed Chapter 53.

A title company will search the records before closing. See Texas property records.

Texas mechanic's lien FAQ

What does a contractor need for a lien on a Texas homestead?

A written contract signed before work begins, signed by both spouses if married, and filed with the county clerk (Property Code Sec. 53.254).

What is the deadline for a residential lien affidavit?

For the original contractor, the 15th day of the third month after the month the work was completed, terminated or abandoned (Sec. 53.052(a)).

How long does a claimant have to sue?

Not later than the first anniversary of the last day to file the affidavit, extendable to the second anniversary of filing by recorded written agreement (Sec. 53.158).

How do I get a lien released after paying?

Request it in writing. The claimant must furnish a recordable release within 10 days after receiving the request (Sec. 53.152).

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What is a mechanic's lien on a Texas home?

A mechanic's lien is a claim against a house, filed by someone who supplied labor or materials and was not paid. Chapter 53 of the Property Code governs it, and a lien claimant has to follow a set of steps for the claim to count.

For a seller, the lien matters because it sits on the title. A buyer's title company will find a recorded lien affidavit, and closing usually will not go ahead until the claim is paid, released, discharged or bonded around.

What makes a lien valid on a homestead?

A homestead gets extra protection. Sec. 53.254 requires several things before a lien can attach to it.

  • A written contract between the owner and the person furnishing labor or materials, signed before the work starts or the material is furnished.
  • Both spouses' signatures if the owner is married.
  • The contract filed with the county clerk of the county where the homestead is located.
  • On the lien affidavit, this notice printed at the top in bold type of at least 10 points: "NOTICE: THIS IS NOT A LIEN. THIS IS ONLY AN AFFIDAVIT CLAIMING A LIEN."
  • For a subcontractor or supplier, a notice to the owner that carries the statutory statement about the 10 percent reserve and withholding.

If a lien fails one of these tests, the owner may be able to have it removed. A contract that was signed after the work began is one example of a defect the statute speaks to directly.

What deadlines apply to a residential lien claim?

The deadlines run to the 15th day of a month and differ for original contractors and for subcontractors or suppliers. Chapter 53 was amended effective January 1, 2022, and the figures below are the current residential ones in the text.

Chapter 53 residential project filing and suit deadlines
StepWhoDeadline
Notice of unpaid claim to owner and original contractor (Sec. 53.056)Subcontractor or supplier15th day of the second month after the month the labor or materials were provided
Lien affidavit with county clerk (Sec. 53.052(a))Original contractor15th day of the third month after the month the work was completed, terminated or abandoned
Lien affidavit with county clerk (Sec. 53.052(c))Subcontractor or supplier15th day of the third month after the month labor or materials were last provided
Copy of the filed affidavit to the owner (Sec. 53.055)Any claimantWithin five days after filing
Suit to foreclose (Sec. 53.158)Any claimantFirst anniversary of the last day to file the lien affidavit, unless extended by a recorded written agreement to no later than the second anniversary of the affidavit date

Count the months from the month of the work, not the day. A claimant who finished in March has until June 15 for a residential lien affidavit as an original contractor, because June is the third month after March.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What does the 10 percent reserve mean for the owner?

During the work and for 30 days after it is completed, the owner must keep back 10 percent of the contract price, or 10 percent of the value of the work done so far (Sec. 53.101). That reserve is the owner's protection against paying twice.

The homestead statement in Sec. 53.254(g) explains the logic. An owner who withheld the reserve, held back enough to cover written claims, and paid that amount to the claimant is not exposed to a valid subcontractor or supplier lien, and apart from the reserve the owner is not liable for money already paid to the contractor before notice of the claim. An owner who skipped the reserve can end up paying the claimants out of pocket.

How does a lien affect a sale of the house?

A recorded lien affidavit puts a cloud on the title that the seller has to deal with before or at closing. Four routes are common, all drawn from Sec. 53.157, which lists the ways an affidavit can be discharged of record.

  • The claimant signs and records a release.
  • The claimant fails to sue within the Sec. 53.158 period.
  • A final court judgment or decree ordering discharge is recorded.
  • A bond is filed under the chapter's bond subchapters, or a certified copy of a court order removing the lien is recorded, as long as the claimant does not post a bond or deposit within 30 days after that order.

Sec. 53.160 lets a party file a verified summary motion in a foreclosure or invalidity suit. Its grounds are limited to defects such as late notice, an affidavit that does not meet Sec. 53.054 or was not filed as Sec. 53.052 requires, or no notice of the filed affidavit.

What bills-paid statement must a seller sign at closing?

When a seller sells a structure of not more than four units that the buyer will use as a principal residence, Sec. 53.259(b) requires the seller to deliver an affidavit at closing. It states that the seller has paid everyone in full for labor and materials used in the construction of improvements, and that the seller owes no one for construction.

If anyone is still owed, the affidavit must state the amount, the name, and if known the address and phone number of each person. A false or misleading statement made intentionally, knowingly or recklessly is a misdemeanor with a fine of up to $4,000, jail up to one year, or both, and the signer is personally liable for resulting loss. For that reason, collect every receipt and release before signing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What should an owner do when a lien shows up?

Start with the dates. Pull the recorded affidavit from the county clerk, note the filing date, and check it against the table above. An affidavit filed after its deadline is one of the defects Sec. 53.160 names.

An owner can also ask in writing for information. Under Sec. 53.159, an owner must answer a written request from someone furnishing labor or materials within a reasonable time and no later than the 10th day, with the legal description, whether there is a surety bond, any prior recorded liens, and the date the original contract was signed.

Finally, make sure the final payment comes with the contractor's bills-paid affidavit required by Sec. 53.259(a). An attorney who handles Texas construction liens can check the notice language and the dates against the recorded paperwork.

More questions about Texas Mechanic's Lien on a Home

Can a contractor put a lien on my Texas homestead?

Yes, but only if a written contract was signed before the work began, both spouses signed if you are married, and the contract was filed with the county clerk. The lien affidavit must also carry the required notice at the top.

How long does a contractor have to file a lien on a house?

An original contractor has until the 15th day of the third month after the month the work was completed, terminated or abandoned. A subcontractor or supplier has until the 15th day of the third month after the month it last furnished labor or materials.

How long does a lien claimant have to sue?

Suit must be brought by the first anniversary of the last day to file the affidavit. A written agreement with the record owner, recorded with the county clerk, can extend that to the second anniversary of the affidavit filing date.

Do I have to keep money back from my contractor?

Yes. Sec. 53.101 requires the owner to reserve 10 percent of the contract price, or of the value of the work, during the work and for 30 days after it is completed.

Can I sell my house while a lien is recorded?

You can contract to sell, but the title company will want the lien released, discharged, bonded or removed first. The bills-paid affidavit at closing must also list any amount still owed.

title: Selling a Rented House in Texas: Landlord and Tenant Rules
content:
Selling a Rented House in Texas: Landlord and Tenant Rules

Cash Home Buyers in Texas
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Selling a Rented House in Texas: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Selling a Rented House in Texas sale
  • Turn the Selling a Rented House in Texas offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Tenant-Occupied House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the property and the lease.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

A Texas landlord cannot lock a tenant out to show or sell a house, and a violation carries a civil penalty of one month's rent plus $1,000. That rule is in Property Code Sec. 92.0081. This guide summarizes the sections of Chapters 91 and 92 we opened that matter when you sell a rented home. We did not find statute text that says a lease survives a sale, so we do not state it.

Ending a month-to-month tenancy

Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy by notice. For a rent period of at least one month, it ends on the later of the day stated in the notice or one month after notice is given (Property Code Sec. 91.001(a) and (b)). A signed agreement can set a different notice period (Sec. 91.001(e)). If a tenancy ends mid-period, the tenant owes rent only to the termination date (Sec. 91.001(d)). Eviction follows its own rules. See the Texas eviction process.

Lockouts and entry

A landlord may not intentionally keep a tenant out of the premises except by judicial process, unless the cause is bona fide repairs, construction or an emergency, removing the contents of abandoned premises, or a lawful lock change for delinquent rent (Sec. 92.0081(b)). A lock-change notice must be mailed locally by the fifth calendar day, or hand-delivered or posted by the third calendar day, before the change (Sec. 92.0081(d)(3)). A violating landlord owes a civil penalty of one month's rent plus $1,000, actual damages, court costs and attorney's fees (Sec. 92.0081(h)).

We did not find a Chapter 92 provision that sets an entry notice period for showings. Entry rules depend on the lease.

We buy tenant-occupied and vacant houses as-is, with no commission.
Get My Cash Offer →

Repairs continue during a sale

A landlord must make a diligent effort to repair a condition that materially affects health or safety once the tenant gives notice and is current on rent (Sec. 92.052(a)), and seven days is presumed a reasonable time (Sec. 92.056(d)). If a new landlord acquires title in good faith by foreclosure, deed in lieu or a bona fide purchase by general warranty deed without knowledge of a tenant's repair notice, the tenant's right to terminate stays in place. For other conditions the tenant must give the new landlord written notice once told the new landlord's name and address (Sec. 92.0562(g)). A new landlord who violates that subsection owes a civil penalty of one month's rent plus $2,000, actual damages and attorney's fees.

Security deposits when you sell

We did not confirm federal protections for tenants at foreclosure, rules on showings and for-sale signs, or cash-for-keys arrangements.

Selling a rented house in Texas FAQ

Can I end a month-to-month lease to sell?

Either party may end it by notice, effective on the later of the date stated or one month after notice, unless a signed agreement sets another period (Property Code Sec. 91.001).

Can I lock a tenant out to show the house?

No. A landlord may not intentionally prevent entry except by judicial process or in listed cases, and a violation carries a civil penalty of one month's rent plus $1,000 (Sec. 92.0081).

What happens to the security deposit when I sell?

The new owner is liable from the date title is acquired and must give the tenant a signed statement with the exact amount (Sec. 92.105).

Does a lease survive a sale?

We found no opened statute text that says so, so we do not state it. Ask a Texas attorney.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Does a tenant stop a Texas owner from selling the rental?

No. A sale of the owner's interest does not remove the tenant, and the lease keeps running while the house changes hands. What changes is who the landlord is, and with that, who answers for the deposit and the lease.

Chapter 92 of the Property Code covers residential landlords and tenants (Sec. 92.002). It does not give a seller a way to clear a tenant out before closing. Any move to end the tenancy has to follow the lease and the eviction process in Chapter 24, so owners often close with the tenant staying put or agree a move date with the tenant.

Who answers for the security deposit after the sale?

The new owner. Sec. 92.105 says that when the owner's interest ends by sale or otherwise, the new owner is liable for deposits from the date title passes.

  • The new owner must hand the tenant a signed statement acknowledging the purchase and the exact dollar amount of the deposit.
  • The former owner stays liable for a deposit received during ownership until the new owner has received it or assumed the liability, absent a different written agreement between the parties.
  • A lender that takes title by foreclosure is excluded from the rule.

In practice, a seller should transfer the deposit at closing and put it on the settlement statement, then get the buyer's signed acknowledgment in writing so the tenant's notice is ready on the day title passes. A tenant's claim to the deposit takes priority over the landlord's creditors, including a trustee in bankruptcy (Sec. 92.103(c)).

What happens to the lease and the rent?

Read the lease for its own terms. The State Law Library explains that a landlord cannot raise the rent before the lease term is up without the tenant's agreement, and that once the term ends there is no state limit on a raise.

A landlord also cannot raise rent in retaliation for repair requests, good faith complaints to a government agency, or tenant organizing (Sec. 92.331, as the library summarizes it). Anyone buying to raise the rent has to wait out the lease and should read it before signing the purchase contract. If the lease is month to month, the buyer's options are different, so ask a Texas real estate attorney.

The lease copy rule also matters when paperwork changes hands. The landlord owes the tenant one full copy of the signed lease to a tenant within three business days (Sec. 92.024), so the buyer should receive the lease with every amendment attached.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What does the tenant get back when the tenancy ends?

Refund is due by day 30 counted from the day the tenant surrenders the premises (Sec. 92.103(a)). A requirement that the tenant give advance notice of surrender works as a condition for the refund only if the lease underlines it or prints it in conspicuous bold.

Deductions are limited to damages and charges the tenant is legally liable for under the lease or because of a breach, and normal wear and tear cannot be kept (Sec. 92.104). When any part is withheld, the landlord sends the balance with a written description and itemized list. This is the account a buyer inherits, which is why a missing deposit record at closing can turn into a dispute months later.

The tenant has duties as well. Sec. 92.108 bars a tenant from withholding the last month's rent on the theory that the deposit covers it. A tenant who does so in bad faith owes three times the rent withheld plus reasonable attorney's fees.

Can a seller show the house to buyers?

Only as far as the lease allows. The state law library says that, Texas has no state law regulating landlord entry, so the lease controls. The lease may require prior notice, and it may name prospective buyers as people who may enter.

If the lease is silent, the landlord may not have a right to enter without permission, apart from emergencies and repairs. Entering more often than necessary, at unreasonable times, or against the lease can breach the tenant's implied right to quiet enjoyment. Ask the tenant for a showing schedule in writing, and keep a record of the agreement.

What can a landlord not do to get the tenant out?

Self help is limited. Sec. 92.008 bars a landlord from interrupting utilities the tenant pays directly, or those the landlord furnishes as part of the tenancy, except for bona fide repairs, construction or an emergency. Sec. 92.0081 bars removing doors, windows, locks or the landlord's furnished appliances other than for bona fide repair, and bars keeping a tenant out except by judicial process or in narrow cases.

One such case is changing the lock of a tenant who is behind on rent. The landlord must then post a written notice on the tenant's front door saying where to get the new key 24 hours a day, and that the landlord must provide it at any hour even if no rent is paid.

A seller who wants possession when the buyer plans to occupy it needs a lawful reason, such as nonrenewal when the lease runs out, or an agreement with the tenant.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

How do notice to vacate and eviction work?

The state law library lays out the court process when a tenant stays past a proper notice. Under Property Code Sec. 24.005, the landlord must give at least three days of written notice to vacate unless the lease sets a longer or shorter one, delivered in person, inside the premises in an obvious place, by mail, or by email if the lease allows it.

Texas eviction timing after notice to vacate
StageTiming
Notice to vacateAt least 3 days if the lease is silent on the period
Suit filed in justice courtHearing set between day 10 and day 21 after filing
Service on the tenantAt least 4 days before trial
Appeal to county courtFive days from judgment
Writ of possessionAvailable 6 days after final judgment, with 24 hours' notice before removal

A federal 30 day notice may apply to some covered properties.

How should an owner prepare a tenant occupied rental for market?

Gather the records first, then decide whether the sale will be while the tenant stays or empty.

  • Collect the lease, amendments, deposit records (Sec. 92.106 requires a landlord to keep accurate deposit records) and rent ledger.
  • Write down the deposit amount and prepare the buyer's signed acknowledgment.
  • Decide how showings will work and ask for access in writing.
  • Pay or prorate property tax. Texas taxes attach as a lien each January 1.
  • Call the appraisal district to learn whether an exemption on the property changes once the sale records.

More questions about Selling a Rented House in Texas

Does the tenant have to leave when I sell the house?

No. The sale does not end the lease. The tenant stays under the lease terms, and the buyer steps in as landlord.

Who gets the security deposit when a rented house is sold?

The new owner is liable for it from the date title passes and must give the tenant a signed statement with the exact amount. The seller stays liable until the buyer receives the deposit or assumes liability.

Can I enter the house to show it to a buyer?

Only as the lease allows. Texas has no statute on landlord entry, so check the lease for a notice requirement and any mention of prospective buyers. If it is silent, get the tenant's permission.

Can I raise the rent before the buyer closes?

Not during the lease term without the tenant's agreement. After the term ends there is no state cap, but a raise cannot be a retaliation for repair requests or complaints.

How long does an eviction take in Texas?

Notice to vacate is at least three days, and the justice court hearing falls 10 to 21 days after filing. A writ of possession is available six days after final judgment, and an appeal has a five day window.

Texas Security Deposit Rules: Refunds, Penalties and What Happens When You Sell

Cash Home Buyers in Texas

Last updated November 14, 2026.

A Texas landlord must refund a security deposit on or before the 30th day after the tenant surrenders the premises, and a landlord who keeps a deposit in bad faith owes $100, three times the amount wrongfully withheld, and the tenant's attorney's fees. Those rules are in Property Code Secs. 92.103 and 92.109. This guide also covers what changes when the owner sells.

Refund and deduction rules

  • A security deposit is an advance of money, other than a rental application deposit or advance rent, meant mainly to secure performance under a dwelling lease (Sec. 92.102).
  • A landlord may deduct damages and charges the tenant is legally liable for, but may not keep any part for normal wear and tear (Sec. 92.104(a) and (b)).
  • If any deposit is kept, the landlord must give the balance with a written description and itemized list of deductions, unless the tenant owes rent at surrender and there is no controversy about the rent (Sec. 92.104(c)).
  • A refund or accounting counts as made if it is mailed and postmarked on or before the due date (Sec. 92.1041).
  • The landlord does not have to return the deposit or send the itemization until the tenant gives a written forwarding address, but the tenant does not lose the refund just for failing to give one (Sec. 92.107).

Penalties

A landlord who keeps a deposit in bad faith is liable for $100, three times the portion wrongfully withheld and the tenant's reasonable attorney's fees. A landlord who in bad faith fails to give the itemized list gives up the right to withhold any deposit or to sue the tenant for damage, and owes attorney's fees (Sec. 92.109). The landlord has the burden to prove the retention was reasonable, and failing to refund or itemize by the 30th day is presumed bad faith. A tenant may not withhold the last month's rent on the ground that the deposit covers it, and a bad-faith violation makes the tenant liable for three times the rent withheld plus attorney's fees (Sec. 92.108).

Selling a tenant-occupied house?
We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant, with no commission.
Get My Cash Offer →

Texas security deposit FAQ

How long does a landlord have to return a security deposit?

On or before the 30th day after the tenant surrenders the premises (Property Code Sec. 92.103(a)).

Can a landlord keep a deposit for normal wear and tear?

No. A landlord may not retain any portion for normal wear and tear (Sec. 92.104(b)).

What is the penalty for keeping a deposit in bad faith?

$100, three times the portion wrongfully withheld and the tenant's reasonable attorney's fees (Sec. 92.109(a)).

Who owes the deposit after a sale?

The new owner is liable from the date title is acquired and must give the tenant a signed statement with the exact amount (Sec. 92.105).

What counts as a security deposit in Texas?

A security deposit is money advanced to secure the tenant's performance under a residential lease, and it is not the same thing as prepaid rent or an application payment. The Texas Property Code draws the lines in Sections 92.102 and 92.351, and the Texas State Law Library repeats them in its landlord and tenant guide.

Getting the label right matters because each kind of payment carries different refund rights. A landlord who calls everything a "deposit" does not change what the statute says about each one. Owners who plan to sell a rental should sort their tenant's payments into the right bucket before anyone asks about a refund.

  • Security deposit: any advance meant mainly to secure performance under a dwelling lease, other than a rental application deposit or advance rent.
  • Application deposit: money given with a rental application that comes back to the applicant if the landlord rejects them.
  • Application fee: a nonrefundable payment that offsets the cost of screening an applicant.

How quickly must a Texas landlord return the deposit?

A landlord must refund the deposit on or before the 30th day after the tenant surrenders the premises. That clock is in Section 92.103 of the Property Code.

There is a condition tied to the forwarding address. Under Section 92.107, the landlord has no duty to return the deposit or send a written description of damages and charges until the tenant gives a written statement of the address to use for the refund. A tenant who forgets to send it does not lose the claim, and may still go to court. The practical step for any tenant is a short dated letter with the new mailing address, kept with a copy.

For a landlord who is mid-sale, this means the 30 days can fall right around a closing date. Calendar the move-out date and the day the written statement arrived, because those two dates drive everything that follows.

What can a landlord deduct from the deposit?

A landlord may deduct damages and charges the tenant is legally liable for under the lease or because the tenant breached it. Section 92.104 also bars keeping any part of the deposit to cover normal wear and tear.

Section 92.001(4) defines normal wear and tear as deterioration from the intended use of the dwelling. It includes breakage or malfunction due to age or a deteriorated condition. It leaves out deterioration caused by negligence, carelessness, accident or abuse by the tenant, a household member, or a guest or invitee.

When a landlord keeps any portion for repairs, an itemized list of every deduction is required if the tenant has paid all rent and no rent dispute exists. Sellers who rent their houses should photograph the unit at move-out and keep the repair invoices, since an itemized list is only as good as the paper behind it.

Which Texas payments are refundable and which are not?

Refund rights depend on the kind of payment, so the quickest way to check is a side by side look at the four payment types the State Law Library describes.

Texas rental payments and how the State Law Library describes them
PaymentWhat it isRefund treatment
Security depositAdvance to secure performance under the leaseRefund due by the 30th day after surrender, less lawful deductions
Application depositMoney given with an applicationRefundable if the applicant is rejected
Application feeScreening cost paymentNonrefundable
Monthly fee in lieu of depositOptional fee paid with rentWritten notice and written record required

Source: Texas State Law Library, Security Deposits.

What can a tenant do about a deposit withheld in bad faith?

A tenant can sue if the deposit or the itemized list has not been mailed within 30 days of moving out. Section 92.109 lets the tenant recover three times the portion of the deposit that was wrongfully withheld, plus other fees.

Where less than $20,000 is at stake, the tenant can file in justice court, and these cases often proceed without lawyers. The State Law Library also lists forms for a refund demand letter and for a lawsuit seeking the deposit. A landlord who is about to sell should treat a pending deposit dispute as a loose end to settle early,.

  • Send the demand letter first and keep proof of delivery.
  • Include the forwarding address in writing.
  • File in justice court if the 30 days pass with no refund or itemized list.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Can a Texas landlord charge a monthly fee instead of a deposit?

Yes. State law lets a landlord offer tenants the choice of paying a monthly fee with the rent instead of putting down a deposit.

The landlord must give written notice of three things: the tenant's right to pay a security deposit instead, the right to stop paying the monthly fee at any point and provide a deposit, and the dollar amount of each option. The choice has to be recorded in writing. If the landlord buys insurance with the fee, the fee cannot exceed the reasonable cost of obtaining and administering that insurance, and a landlord who files an insurance claim cannot also bill the tenant for the same damage.

A buyer reviewing a rental should ask which arrangement each tenant has, since a fee-based lease has no deposit to hand over at closing.

What happens to tenants and deposits when you sell a Texas rental?

Selling a tenant-occupied house does not erase the tenant's deposit claim, so gather the paperwork before you list. Ask your closing attorney or title company how the deposit will be handled in the contract, and put that answer in writing.

A useful file contains the signed lease, the amount and date of each payment, any written notice about a monthly fee, and the move-out photos. If you need the property empty, the process is separate from the deposit. Property Code Section 24.005 generally calls for at least three days' written notice to vacate unless the lease says otherwise, and eviction suits go to justice court. The State Law Library's eviction page lays out the steps, including the five-day window to appeal to county court.

  • Hand the buyer copies of every lease and deposit record.
  • Do not deduct for ordinary wear and tear from the tenant's deposit.
  • Ask the county clerk or your attorney about anything you are unsure of.

What records should a Texas landlord keep about each deposit?

Keep the signed lease, proof of the amount and date received, the move-in condition photos, and every written notice the tenant sends, including the forwarding address. These records are what you will rely on if the tenant files in justice court.

Because the refund clock runs 30 days from the day the tenant surrenders the premises, note that date in writing as well. A short log with the surrender date, the date the forwarding address arrived, the date the refund or itemized list went out, and the method of delivery gives you a clear timeline. Landlords with several rentals tend to lose track of these dates, and a buyer's lawyer reviewing the rental file will ask for the same documents.

More questions about Texas Security Deposit Rules

Is there a statewide cap on a Texas security deposit?

The State Law Library pages for this topic do not state a cap, so check the lease and ask a Texas attorney or your local justice court clerk. What the pages do cover is the refund deadline, the deductions and the penalty for bad faith.

Does the tenant have to give notice of a forwarding address?

Yes, in writing, if they want the landlord's refund duty to start. Section 92.107 says the landlord need not return the deposit or describe damages until the tenant provides a written forwarding address, though a tenant who skips it keeps the right to sue.

Can a landlord keep the deposit for ordinary carpet wear?

No. Section 92.104 bars keeping deposit money for normal wear and tear, which covers deterioration from intended use. Damage from negligence, accident or abuse is treated differently.

How much can a tenant recover for a bad faith withholding?

Three times the wrongfully withheld portion of the deposit, plus other fees, under Section 92.109. Suits under $20,000 can be filed in justice court.

Do I need to settle deposits before I sell a rental house?

Yes, plan for it. Collect the lease and payment records, decide with your closing attorney how the deposit is handled, and keep a written record, because the tenant's refund rights do not disappear when a sale is signed.
